stem.text: Compound Z, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{13}\text{Br}$, has two chiral centres. A sample of Z contains all four possible optical isomers.
This sample of Z reacts with hot ethanolic $\text{NaOH}$ to produce a mixture of **only** three isomers. Two of these isomers are optical isomers of each other.
What could be the formula of Z?

A.alt: Skeletal formula of a cyclohexane ring carrying one Br and one CH3 group on adjacent carbons

B.alt: Skeletal formula of a cyclohexane ring carrying one Br and one CH3 group

C.alt: Skeletal formula of a cyclopentane ring carrying one Br and two CH3 groups

D.alt: Skeletal formula of a cyclobutane ring carrying one Br and three CH3 groups
